criteria_source: The fixture only. schema.sql states the stack is PostgreSQL 16 with about 38,000 products growing by a few hundred a month; Postgres full-text search (tsvector with a GIN index) and pg_trgm are stock capabilities of that version at that scale. Written from the fixture, not from rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the search runs in the PostgreSQL the service already has - full-text search over name and description with a tsvector and GIN index, or pg_trgm similarity - which handles 38,000 rows comfortably. Fails when it recommends standing up a separate search engine (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Algolia, Meilisearch, Typesense) as the build without establishing that the existing database cannot serve this scale, or hand-rolls an application-side inverted index, or proposes only LIKE '%term%' with no index strategy and no mention of Postgres's built-in full-text support.
